messages:
elena: Heads-up — AcmePay opened an escalation: p99 for streaming responses jumped this week. Non-streaming (sync) endpoints are fine, but customers see the first chunk/TTFB delayed by ~2–3s. Happens on HTTP/2 path.

elena: Their quick repro (they sent this):
```
# streaming (SSE) via http2 — slow first byte
curl -v -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams -d '{"prompt":"hello"}' --http2 -N

# non-streaming — ok
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/completions -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'
```

kevin: thanks — can you grab a request id + upstream logs (nginx/ingress) for one of the slow requests? also which region and customer plan (hosted/dedicated)?

elena: request_id=rx-20260310-ACME-01, region=us-west-2, hosted. Attached trace snippet from our edge:
```
edge: recv -> 12.345s -> proxied to runtime
runtime: accepted -> 12.348s -> started generating first tokens
runtime: first flush -> 0.1s after generation
edge: returned first bytes -> 2.9s after proxied (coalesced)
```

maya: that pattern screams proxy coalescing on the HTTP/2 path. many proxies will reframe small chunks into larger frames or buffer until a window/threshold. HTTP/1.1 + chunked typically preserves flushes better.

sasha: agreed. do we have any ingress/proxy (ALB/nginx/Cloudflare) rules that differ between streaming and sync routes? sometimes we have an http2-only listener for /streams.

elena: their path hits our h2-terminating edge (Cloudfront -> nginx -> runtime). nginx config for that vhost has proxy_buffering on by default.

sasha: quick mitigation options (low risk):
- route streaming traffic to HTTP/1.1 SSE listener (bypass http2 coalescing)
- set proxy_buffering off for the streaming vhost
- increase internal flush threshold at runtime so the first flush contains a small prefix (so coalescing is less painful)

kevin: long-term we should:
- teach smart-router to prefer http/1.1 for SSE/generic streaming clients (config flag)
- expose a runtime knob `stream.preflush_threshold` to force an immediate small flush after model warmup/prefix tokens
- add metric: streaming_ttfb - sync_ttfb delta (p50/p95/p99) per route

elena: trying the simple tests now. @acme on call said they'd try curl --http1.1 with -N as well, will report.

deploy-bot: canary deploy queued for change "runtime: expose stream.preflush_threshold" on canary cluster c-2. ETA 20m.

support-bot: note added to ticket ACME-3421: "Investigate TTFB delta on streaming h2 vs http1"

maya: nginx snippet that helped another customer — disables buffering + forces chunked transfer:
```nginx
location /v1/streams {
  proxy_buffering off;
  proxy_http_version 1.1;
  chunked_transfer_encoding on;
  proxy_set_header Connection ""; # allow keepalive
}
```

kevin: thanks. also, if we can't change edge config immediately, we can implement a runtime fallback: if streaming request is over HTTP/2 and ttfb > 1.5s, server can return a short 1–2 token prefix and then pause for a tick, or return a 303 to a /streams-http1 endpoint (ugh but works).

elena: update from Acme: they tried `curl --http1.1 -N` and p99 TTFB dropped from ~2.9s -> ~0.3s. So proxy coalescing confirmed.

sasha: good repro. plan:
1) short-term (today): set proxy_buffering off for /v1/streams on edge (config rollout to edge-nodes in us-west/region) — low risk.
2) medium (days): enable router rule to prefer http/1.1 for streaming routes.
3) longer (weeks): runtime flag to preflush and product docs for recommended client flags (curl -N, SSE, disable http2 if using proxies that coalesce).

kevin: I'll land the runtime flag change behind a feature flag (deploy-bot already queued canary). also adding an alarm in telemetry: if (streaming_p99_ttfb - sync_p99_ttfb) > 1s for 5m, page eng-runtime oncall.

elena: I'm rolling the nginx change to the us-west streaming vhost now and will monitor. will post results in 10–15m.

elena: quick post-deploy: after disabling proxy_buffering on the vhost, Acme's p99 TTFB dropped to 0.35s for streaming. They confirm UX restored.

maya: awesome. action items assigned:
- sasha: PR for router rule to prefer http/1.1 for /v1/streams (review by kevin)
- kevin: merge runtime preflush flag behind feature-flag + telemetry + alert rule
- elena: add KB to support docs showing curl repro and suggested mitigations (nginx snippet, curl --http1.1 -N, client keepalive guidance)

sasha: I'll open the PR today.

kevin: leaving a note for postmortem: why did this regression spike now? hypothesis: recent change to edge h2 frame coalescing upgrade (perf patch) + load shift that made coalescing thresholds hit more often. we'll dig into edge change logs.

elena: thanks everyone — closing the customer loop now. I'll attach the KB and mark the ticket resolved once the router rule PR is in canary. :tada:
